Jaleel's book had a constructive session today: 14 of 19 holdings rose. The biggest lifts came from AstraZeneca (+2.99%, after the TEZSPIRE Phase III EoE trial met its co-primary endpoints), Adobe (+3.32%), S&P Global (+2.34%) and Boston Scientific (+1.13%). The tape was a rotation out of AI-exposed names into established cash-flow businesses, which helped Adobe and S&P. The same Fed-hike worries hit chips, with NVIDIA down 0.31% and Broadcom flat at -0.01%. The main drag was Abbott, down 1.55% at a 10.6% weight. Unrealized P&L for the book stands at -1.33%.

Price and thesis are diverging in a few places. Rocket Lab is -34.9% on a 5.5% weight and rated AVOID (QARP 36.6). Lululemon (-22.1%) and Nike are also AVOID, and today's bounces in both don't change that. Boston Scientific is rated STRONG BUY (QARP 79.2) but carries an elevated flag: FY26 growth was cut from 10.5% to 7–8.5%, with management guiding flat through Q3. Adobe's pop looks like rotation rather than a fix for the AI-moat fear.

Next on the calendar: Abbott reports tomorrow, Wednesday Oct 21, and Boston Scientific follows on Oct 28. Equifax jumped 11.29% on a 0.8% weight, and the headline supplied doesn't explain it.
